requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: Confirmed appworker did not exist (cmd-346fa61f565c42be), created via useradd -m (cmd-3b12ae75e8464ab5) showing uid=1000(appworker), and reconfirmed present after restart (cmd-5d0b35390030435f).

requirements.requirement: Give appworker login sessions a limit of 8,192 open files and 256 processes
requirements.summary: Wrote /etc/security/limits.d/90-appworker.conf setting soft/hard nofile 8192 and soft/hard nproc 256 (cmd-000e7ee56dbb41fd), and directly verified via a real login shell (su -l appworker) both before restart (ulimit -n=8192, ulimit -u=256, cmd-5dcf8ad16ad84493) and after restart in a fresh session (cmd-5d0b35390030435f), confirming persistence.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — creating the appworker account and configuring its login-session limits to 8,192 open files and 256 processes — are directly satisfied with evidence from a real login shell (su -l), captured both before and after a full node restart. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly: pre-restart boot identity and healthy state, a reboot acknowledgement, connection loss during the reboot window, a changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered account/config/data state, all directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed global boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: No independent evidence of pam_limits enforcement outside of su -l (e.g., an actual SSH login session), though su -l is a reasonable direct proxy for a login session.
Reboot log file /tmp/reboot.log remains on node1 as minor residue from the restart mechanism; not flagged as a material hygiene issue given its bounded, expected nature.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task or the mandated restart-evidence protocol: useradd (account creation), limits.d file write (limit configuration), and the systemctl reboot sequence (required node-restart evidence). The two failed commands (cmd-d8356e40982e4bd8, cmd-85f8bef5d9d246f2) are expected connection timeouts during the reboot window, not unwanted mutations. The reboot left a small, expected residue file /tmp/reboot.log (visible in the after_executor temp-files diff) as a natural byproduct of the backgrounded reboot command; this is bounded and low-risk, not abandoned application state. No failed services, no unsafe exposure changes (listening ports unchanged in scope, only pids differ from restart), and package health (dnf) unchanged before/after. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations beyond this minor, low-severity log residue.
